title: Ultraviolet shell makes an order-one point-variance deficit cost order N^4

shell_cost.shell: For the standard three-dimensional torus cutoff, take the real-mode shell S_N={j:N/2<=|k_j|_infinity<=N}; it has Theta(N^3) modes, omega_j=Theta(N), lambda_j=(2omega_j)^(-1)=Theta(N^-1), and free covariance mass C_(S,N)=sum_(S_N)lambda_j>=kappa C_N for some cutoff-independent kappa>0 and all large N
shell_cost.low_variance_deficit: If v_N=sum_j lambda_j s_j<=(kappa/2)C_N, then v_(S,N)<=v_N and delta_(S,N)=sum_(S_N)lambda_j(1-s_j)>=C_(S,N)-v_N>=kappa C_N/2=Theta(N^2)
shell_cost.dual_shell_bound: On S_N, lambda_j/omega_j=O(N^-2), so sum_(S_N)lambda_j^2 s_j/omega_j<=O(N^-2)v_(S,N)=O(1)
shell_cost.free_cost_consequence: The squeeze part of q0 is one quarter of the first Cauchy factor, hence q0[psi_(alpha,s)]>=cN^4 whenever v_N<=(kappa/2)C_N
shell_cost.high_variance_consequence: If v_N>(kappa/2)C_N, K1524's optimized Wick expectation is at least c C_N^2=cN^4 whether v_N lies below or above C_N
shell_cost.scope_guard: The shell proof uses stationary translation-invariant diagonal covariance and the native three-dimensional spectral cutoff; it is not a lower bound for arbitrary Gaussian or non-Gaussian states
